We made reservations at Spoon and Stable for an earlier brunch over the weekend. Quite frankly, we were trying to get reservations for dinner but it was completely sold out for several days in advance. We were still happy to get a brunch reservation.

Upon arrival were greeted and even though we were 15 minutes early the hostess was able to get us seated immediately.

The atmosphere and vibe of the restaurant is very open, with plenty of tables and booths. The kitchen is open concept, so you can see the chefs preparing the food. I highly recommend getting reservations, as it was a very full restaurant.

Our waiter was very fun, friendly, and explained the menu perfectly. The menu also clearly marks what is gluten free, vegetarian and several dairy free which was great to see.

The biggest score was the gluten free chicken & waffles, made with sorghum and served with spiced honey butter & chicken. It is not very often you find a gluten free version of chicken & waffles.

The French dip with roast beef, horseradish cream, Gruyere, and caramelized onion was also very good, served with a side of French fries.

However, what really won us over were the pastries. They were on display, and once we were looking at them, we could not help ourselves and took some to go.

The banana bread, which is both gluten free and dairy free, was extraordinarily good. Moist and delicious. The cinnamon cardamom roll was heavenly, fluffy, and had just the right amount of cardamom.

I can see why this place gets such high reviews, and I would really like to try it for dinner next time I am in Minneapolis.

Lovely restaurant, delicious food! We came here on a Friday night with our two kids and a friend and had a wonderful dinner! The weather was perfect, so there were a number of folks dining outside. We ended up sitting inside and I was surprised and pleased that they had an actual table set for 5 (most places convert 4 or 6 person settings).

We started with the carrot tarator, which our kids really enjoyed. It was a nice, light starter. Our server recommended we order from the Turkish Cuisine, since that was their specialty, and it did not disappoint. My husband got the Chicken Shish Kebab, which was phenomenal! I got the Veggie Hunkar Begendi, which was also delicious and full of vegetables! I am not a fan of mushrooms, but the mushrooms were good, I must say.

They have a super small kids small, essentially just a burger and chicken tenders, which our kids each ordered, and which came with some really good fries. Really satisfied with our meal and would highly recommend to anyone in the area!

I visited Lumi Restaurant during a work conference and stopped in for lunch because I wanted to try Turkish food for the first time. From the moment I walked in, I was genuinely surprised by how warm, inviting, and thoughtfully put together the space was. The restaurant felt incredibly clean and had such positive, welcoming vibes.

The service was fantastic. My friend and I happened to be the only guests there at the time, so we really got what felt like a white-glove experience. The menu was attractive and concise—enough variety to be interesting without feeling overwhelming.

We were started with warm, puffy bread and creamy hummus, which was light, savory, and a really fun way to begin the meal.

For my entrée, I ordered the Beef Guvec, and all I can say is—flavor bomb. The beef was incredibly tender, and the chickpeas paired perfectly with the long-grain rice between bites. Every element of the dish felt comforting, rich, and well balanced. Sorry, no pictures of the actual entrée because I inhaled it.

I also ordered Turkish tea, which was served warm and had a fresh, clean black tea taste that paired beautifully with the meal.

What stood out just as much as the food was the kindness and respect from our server. The hospitality truly made the experience memorable.

This was such a great first introduction to Turkish cuisine, and I’ll absolutely be back. I didn’t catch our server’s name, but if you’re reading this—you know who you are. Thank you for making our visit so enjoyable.

From the moment we arrived, we were genuinely impressed by the inviting atmosphere and the beautifully designed interior, which created a very pleasant setting for our dinner.

However, our experience with the service and certain aspects of the meal was somewhat mixed. Out  order was taken by the bartender (who was busy at her service)  In contrast, other waitstaff seemed less engaged, often congregating near the podium. This became particularly evident after we finished our main courses, as we found ourselves waiting for a significant period before having to actively seek out a server to request our bill.

Regarding the food, our overall impression was unfortunately average, with some dishes being quite disappointing. We ordered the Cashville Salmon and the Pimento Cheese Steak. While the Cashville Salmon was satisfactory, it didn't particularly stand out. The Pimento Cheese Steak was excessively salty, which unfortunately masked any other potential flavors and made it rather unappetizing. The accompanying avocado potato salad also failed to impress, as its taste and texture were not particularly appealing.

On a highly positive note, the cocktails were great!

We started with oysters (oysters are oysters, always solid), and then we tried the potato churros and wow. I did not expect that at all. They were basically the best version of a french fry I’ve ever had in my life.

Next up was the beef tongue bruschetta, and that one really surprised me too. I love beef tongue and think it’s one of the most underrated cuts, but I’d never had it presented like that. It was genuinely delicious and had a mix of flavors I’ve never had before.

It’s very hard to find pasta in Minnesota that really impresses you like that, but this one did. The parmesan quality was obvious, rich, sharp, and just perfect with the pepper. Best cacio e pepe style pasta I’ve ever had, hands down.

On top of all that, Nathan took care of us and made the whole experience even better. Great service, super attentive, and the food runners were genuinely kind too. Overall, an awesome night and a meal I’m still thinking about.

I think Bucheron is overhyped. Our food was pretty good and the service was excellent but I couldn’t help but feel a bit disappointed with the overall experience. When we walked in we were hit with an overwhelming odor of urine that lingered throughout the meal. I wish we had asked to sit outside. I don’t care how good the food is, it isn’t super enjoyable if you feel like you’re eating in a portapotty.

The foie gras was good but I think there was more butter/fat in it than actual chicken liver. It ate more like a chicken liver flavored butter than like a terrine which it claimed to be on the menu. The venison tartare was also good but it was served slightly chilled rather than cold and while the flavor was nice, almost room temperature raw meat isn’t super enjoyable.

The lobster spaghetti and Wagyu flatiron were delicious and I wish we had just gotten those and skipped the apps.

Our server was great. She was super friendly and helped me pick out a drink when I was being indecisive and it was very good. However, the experience was ruined for us because the table seated inches away from us was so loud and obnoxious we could hardly hold a conversation ourselves. I know the restaurant can’t control that but that is a risk you run when you place tables so close together. Considering the bill was over $300 for two people, I’d expect a more upscale atmosphere.

I’m not from the area but I would not see myself returning here if I was. This was a rare miss for James Beard.

Because this  restaurant was no longer available,  we ate at the Butcher 's Tale a couple of times in the last few years and it turned out to be a  pleasant experience with a very memorable dessert- the chocolate cake.  My  husband discovered this restaurant was opened again so he wanted to take me here for our anniversary thinking it will be better than the Butcher 's Tale. It was distracting loud at times and the awkwardness of someone watching over us.
We ordered the grill oysters for appetizer and very disappointing.  The flavor was good but the oysters were small and shrunk into barely enough for a bite.  The chorizo sausage was good by itself and the Mexican corn was okay on its own, they were served together on the same plate so the flavor was overwhelming for me. My husband liked the dish. Did we not ordered the right items? The waitress praised we made the right choice lol. I don't plan on coming back anytime soon.

This was a great spot for a Valentine's Day dinner because the atmosphere was on point and the food quality was good. The decor was designed for couples to have a good time going on dates, and the noise level is good enough for people to not have to yell. My partner and I definitely had a good time here on that day.

Straight from the Valentine's Day menu, I ordered the blood orange cosmo drink, which was essentially a vodka and champagne mix with fruity flavor, and it worked very well for my taste buds. My partner got the lump crab croquettes and we enjoyed it a lot because the béarnaise sauce and the asparagus emulsion provided two layers of flavors, and both worked very well with the croquettes. The escargots didn't really have much of a taste, so it was mainly the texture that carried the dish while the butter à la bourguignonne, which really is just garlic butter, provided some flavor. The beet salad had good taste because of the candied walnuts, the vinaigrette, goat cheese, and the apples, but the beets were a bit too chewy and personally I would have preferred it to be a bit softer (boil it first), but that's just a personal preference as the dish was still great. For the French onion soup, the gruyere cheese on the top that made it look overflowing was visually appealing. There wasn't really a highlight in terms of its taste, though. The croque monsieur, which is really just ham and cheese sandwich, tasted good in the most classic way, and the gruyere cheese helped. Finally, the crème brûlée was made pretty well, with the burnt candy on top not too hard to break and the mixture containing good taste with toasted hazelnuts providing an extra layer of flavor and texture to the dessert.

Eve did a great job serving us that evening as well!  She was attentive to our needs and ensure checking on us when we needed her. Overall this is a good spot for a date. Not every dish was perfect, but most of them were and I think this is a spot worth going back to.

We recently visited Union Rooftop for a special dinner to celebrate my daughter’s birthday after hearing great things, and while the experience had some highlights, the food ultimately didn’t live up to expectations.

Making a reservation online was simple, and I was pleasantly surprised that we were seated right away, I had fully expected a wait even with a reservation. The rooftop restaurant itself is beautiful and has a great atmosphere, though it was crowded and the tables felt a bit close together.

I started with an Old Fashioned, which unfortunately was disappointing. It came with crushed ice, which watered it down quickly and took away from the quality of the drink. We ordered cheese curds as an appetizer, and those were a hit, hot, gooey, and full of flavor.

One of the standout parts of the evening was our waitress. She was absolutely amazing attentive, kind, and knowledgeable. If this review were based on her service alone, it would easily be 5 stars. I just wish I had caught her name because she truly made a positive impression.

The biggest letdown was the entrees. My daughters ordered the gnocchi and Cajun Alfredo, and I ordered the hanger steak special. My steak was much rarer than I prefer, but I tried to eat it anyway. After a few bites of tough, chewy meat, I had to send it back. Our waitress immediately noticed the issue as well. I ended up ordering the chicken wild rice soup instead, which was comforting and enjoyable.

Since we were celebrating my daughter’s birthday, she received a cute dessert, which was a nice touch. Unfortunately, one of my daughters felt sick after eating her gnocchi, which really put a damper on the night, she is not a fan of pasta anymore.

Overall, the experience felt fancy and visually impressive, but the food didn’t match the high expectations. There were definitely bright spots, especially the service, but for the price and reputation, we had hoped for a much better dining experience.

My two friends and I visited Union Rooftop for brunch yesterday, and overall we had a wonderful experience. The food was delicious, the atmosphere was great, and most importantly, the service from our assigned server, Giovanni, was exceptional. He was attentive, professional, and made us feel very welcome throughout our visit.

The only disappointing part of our experience involved another employee who was wearing a green dress. She removed the umbrella from our table and moved it to another table whose guests had just arrived, leaving my friend sitting directly under the hot sun. When we politely asked her not to move it, her response was rude and dismissive. She simply said, “Well, you have to share,” without showing any concern for our comfort. Her customer service skills left much to be desired and did not reflect the level of hospitality we experienced from the rest of the staff.

Despite this unfortunate interaction, I am still leaving a 5-star review because I refuse to let one employee overshadow an otherwise excellent experience. The food was fantastic, Giovanni provided outstanding service, and we genuinely enjoyed our brunch. I would gladly return and hope management addresses situations like this in the future.

Multiple servers checked on us throughout the evening, making sure we had everything we needed. I’ve never received such attentive service while sitting at the bar.

We ordered a bottle of wine from Italy, which was excellent, and the arancini were spectacular. For our entrées, we had the Mafalda Bolognese and the Pasta Carbonara. Both dishes were wonderful, but if I had to choose a favorite, it would be the Mafalda the red sauce was outstanding.

We ended the meal with a cheesecake which was the perfect finish. Overall, it was a fantastic dining experience and a great way to end the day.

Do yourself a favor and get here as soon as possible you wont regret the decision or that you waited so long.

Since we planned on having dinner there, we asked to be moved because it would have been difficult to eat and cut our food. She never asked if we needed anything else or if we wanted a refill, even though our water glasses had been empty for 10 to 15 minutes.

At the end of the meal, the check was brought out without asking how we wanted to split it. There were four of us, two couples, so obviously one person wasn't paying for the entire bill.

I will never be back, and I won't recommend this restaurant to anyone. For a restaurant in such a nice hotel, I'm honestly disgusted.

text.text:
Our recent dining experience at 112 was nothing short of exceptional, and it’s one we’ll be talking about for quite some time. From the moment we sat down, the tone was set by our server, who was not only attentive and knowledgeable but also genuinely enthusiastic about the menu. They offered several recommendations, and in a moment of adventurous enthusiasm, we decided to order all of them—no regrets there! It turned into a fun and memorable experience, and honestly, it’s the kind of place where you want to try everything anyway.

To start, we ordered a variety of appetizers to share, including the lamb chops, prawns, broccoli, and French fries. Nearly everything that came out was outstanding. The lamb chops were tender, flavorful, and cooked to perfection, while the prawns had a great texture and were seasoned beautifully. Even the broccoli, which can sometimes feel like an afterthought at other restaurants, was elevated into something truly delicious. The only minor disappointment among the starters was the French fries. While not terrible, they lacked the crispness you’d hope for and came across a bit soggy, especially compared to how strong everything else was. That said, it was a small blemish on an otherwise fantastic lineup.

For the main courses, the kitchen absolutely delivered. I ordered a pasta and lamb dish that completely exceeded expectations—it was rich, perfectly balanced, and incredibly satisfying. The flavors were bold without being overwhelming, and the portion size was generous enough that I left feeling fully content. It’s one of those dishes you keep thinking about long after the meal is over.

My wife and her mom both chose the halibut, and it was a hit on both fronts. They couldn’t stop talking about how fresh it tasted and how well it was prepared. The portions were more than adequate, and the quality was evident in every bite. We also shared the skirt steak, which deserves special recognition—it was easily one of the standout items of the night. Cooked exactly right and packed with flavor, it’s a dish I would return for without hesitation.

The drinks were just as enjoyable as the food. Cocktails were well-crafted, and the beer was served ice cold—always appreciated. It rounded out the meal perfectly and added to the overall relaxed, enjoyable atmosphere.

All in all, 112 delivered an outstanding dining experience. With the exception of the slightly underwhelming fries, every dish impressed, and the service elevated the evening even further. It’s a place that clearly takes pride in both its food and hospitality, and it shows in every detail. We’ll absolutely be back.

Food was 4.5 stars, service was 100/10. The service and ambience at this place was so spectacular that I felt like I was in a magical candlelit oasis being served food by a fairy who knew everything I wanted.
Our waitress Gracie was such a vibe and did an amazing job that elevated our experience to 5 stars. This was a perfect date night spot to celebrate our 4 year anniversary, and they gave us 2 rounds of champagne on the house to help us celebrate.

The food tasted amazing, was presented beautifully, and none of the dishes disappointed. Our favorite dishes were the SAUTÉED WILD ATLANTIC SALMON and the SOURDOUGH & PARSNIP BRUSCHETTA (runner up SEARED SEA SCALLOPS). All 3 of these had us looking at each other in amazement with every bite. The other dishes we had were great, but less life changing. I’d say the TOASTED RYE & BUTTERMILK CREPE is skippable.

Even the bathroom was bougie, and all of the staff impressively knew every detail about the complicated dishes being served to us.
While Dario’s doppio and mushrooms were more life changing than what we had here, Alma is overtaking it to be my new #1 favorite restaurant.

text.text: I've walked by a few times and decided to go in today.  I went with the philly as that seems to be the star of the menu.  Full size is $20 which seems high; however, it does come with fries and a drink.  I sat down waiting for food to cook and the place is clean, tidy, and well kept.  Service was good, very kind and friendly.  The reason I'm giving 3 stars is due to the kitchen staff having a loud discussion and swearing pretty constantly.  Normal kitchen staff behavior, but not when the witch is front of house.  I took my food back to the office to eat.  The food was great.  Sandwich had good flavor and was massive...half was almost more than I could eat, so two meals out of this thing.  I also upgraded from fries to cheese curds and they loaded me up...I do wish there was an option for mushrooms and jalapenos on the philly- that would have topped it off for sure.  Also, having some au jus would be a nice option.  Overall, great stop for lunch, could have easily split with a coworker.  Would be great to add another side option for those of us who prefer something not fried.

highlightedText.text: "The atmosphere and taste of the dishes created an upscale experience;"

text.text: The concept (focus on local sources and ingredients, hospitality-included price) attracted me to book a reservation for my and my partner's last dinner on our trip to Minneapolis.  The atmosphere and taste of the dishes created an upscale experience; the only dish that seemed unbalanced was the "Crispy Mung Bean Griddle Cakes" (Asian ingredients all have distinct personalities, so it takes a deft hand to balance them to be harmonious vs. cacophonous).  Our server was professional, genuine, and friendly.  The main disruptor to our otherwise pleasant experience was biting down on what was a small broken piece of gray plastic in the beet "rillette."  We showed it to our server with a sincere request to show it to the kitchen staff to discover the cause and ensure mindfulness for dishes they will serve to customers going forward; she apologized, took the $5pp bread course cost off our bill, and said the prep team wasn't onsite but that she would share the feedback.  It's a lovely restaurant that I hope will focus on ensuring that their operational execution is as elevated as the concept, and continue to thrive.
